mechanism_narrative: Sustained decline in RETAIL_REC from -11.6% to -22.9% over four weeks signals accelerating consumer avoidance of retail venues. This downward momentum persists into the next four weeks, producing further negative RETAIL_REC change.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined 11.3 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has recovered from -59.0% to -32.0% over two weeks, indicating partial return to office activity. This workplace recovery drives weekday retail foot traffic within one week, lifting RETAIL_REC above its current depressed baseline.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises more than 15 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 27 points from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase in the week immediately following a WORKPLACES surge of >15 points in more than 40% of observed instances.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility collapsed from 21.6% to -8.9% over two weeks, signaling loss of outdoor recreational substitutes for retail. Consumers redirect discretionary activity back to indoor retail venues, reversing RETAIL_REC decline over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines more than 20 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell 30.5 points from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its t-0w level for all four weeks following the PARKS collapse.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT stations remain severely depressed at -55.9%, constraining consumer access to retail districts. Persistent transit suppression acts as a binding constraint on RETAIL_REC recovery regardless of other signals, keeping RETAIL_REC negative over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -50% for four consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -55.9% for three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases above its four-week mean despite TRANSIT remaining below -50% throughout the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stabilized near +1.9% to +10.7%, indicating essential-goods shopping remains steady. Consumers making regular grocery trips increase incidental retail purchases during the same trips, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above +1% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM positive in all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines further despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining positive and stable.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility elevated at +12.7% signals sustained home-based activity and reduced outdoor mobility. When combined with TRANSIT suppression at -55.9%, this indicates consumers are confined to residential areas and unable to access retail, producing continued RETAIL_REC decline.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above +10% AND TRANSIT below -50% simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at +12.7% and TRANSIT at -55.9% in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next four weeks when RESIDENTIAL remains elevated and TRANSIT remains suppressed.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES recovery from -59.0% to -32.0% combined with PARKS collapse from +21.6% to -8.9% indicates a seasonal shift away from outdoor activity toward work-centered routines. This regime shift produces a four-week rebound in RETAIL_REC as commuting patterns normalize.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises >20 points AND PARKS falls >20 points within two weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES +27 points and PARKS -30.5 points over two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next 28 days despite concurrent WORKPLACES recovery and PARKS decline.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC decline accelerates (-11.6% to -22.9%) while GROCERY_PHARM remains resilient (+1.9% to +10.7%), indicating consumers are substituting essential shopping for discretionary retail. This substitution pattern intensifies over one week, deepening RETAIL_REC losses before potential reversal.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC declines >5 points week-on-week while GROCERY_PHARM remains positive
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell 4.0 points from t-1w to t-0w while GROCERY_PHARM fell only 4.7 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases in the week following a divergence between RETAIL_REC decline and GROCERY_PHARM stability.
